result:
The library at midnight is not truly silent. It breathes. The books settle like old birds in nests of paper and glue, dreaming of hands that once held them. Outside, rain taps the tall windows in patient Morse code, asking to be let in. I walk between the shelves with no lantern, guided by the faint phosphorescence of titles, each spine a small sleeping animal.

Here are the maps of impossible countries, folded into atlases that smell of cinnamon and dust. Here are the letters never sent, pressed between biographies of people who forgot their own names. A dictionary mutters in its sleep, rearranging definitions so that loneliness briefly means the sound of a clock forgetting to tick.

I find an empty chair beside a globe. Its oceans are painted a green so hopeful it makes me ache. I sit and open a book I did not choose. The pages are blank at first, then slowly ink rises like tea leaves, forming a sentence: You are not lost; you are merely being read.

Somewhere above, the ceiling becomes a planetarium. Constellations arrange themselves into words in languages I almost remember. I understand, in the way one understands weather, that every story ever abandoned leaves a residue, a quiet gravity.

When dawn finally slips under the door, the library exhales. I close the book. My hands are warm. Outside, the rain has become ordinary again, but I carry its secret rhythm home, and listen to the shelves whispering softly behind me.
